description:
A state is planning its electricity capacity for the next several years. The state has a forecast of the demand for electricity each year, which is presumed to be accurate. Currently, there are existing oil-fired power plants that will continue to operate and provide some of the needed electricity.
To meet the growing demand, the state is considering building either coal-fired or nuclear power plants. Building coal plants costs a certain amount per unit of capacity, and similarly, building nuclear plants has its own cost per unit of capacity.
However, there are limitations. For political and safety reasons, the state has decided that nuclear power should not exceed a certain percentage of the total electricity capacity. Additionally, coal plants have a certain lifespan, after which they will no longer be operational, and the same goes for nuclear plants.
The goal is to figure out the most cost-effective plan to expand electricity capacity by deciding how much to invest in coal and nuclear plants each year, while adhering to the constraints on nuclear power and considering the lifespan of each type of plant.

Demand.definition: Demand for electricity in each time period

OilCap.definition: Available capacity from existing oil-fired plants in each time period

CoalCost.definition: Cost per unit of capacity for building a coal plant

NukeCost.definition: Cost per unit of capacity for building a nuclear plant

MaxNuke.definition: Maximum fraction of total capacity that can be nuclear

CoalLife.definition: Lifespan of a coal plant in time periods

NukeLife.definition: Lifespan of a nuclear plant in time periods

objective.description: "Minimize the total investment cost of building coal-fired and nuclear power plant capacity over the planning horizon while meeting electricity demand and policy constraints."

constraints.description: For each time period, the total available capacity (oil-fired capacity plus active coal capacity plus active nuclear capacity) must be at least equal to the electricity demand in that period
For each time period, the active nuclear capacity must not exceed MaxNuke times the total available capacity (oil-fired plus active coal plus active nuclear capacity)
In each time period, the active coal capacity is equal to the sum of coal capacities built in the current and previous CoalLife - 1 periods (i.e., coal plants operate only for CoalLife periods)

In each time period, the active nuclear capacity is equal to the sum of nuclear capacities built in the current and previous NukeLife - 1 periods (i.e., nuclear plants operate only for NukeLife periods)
The amount of coal and nuclear capacity built in each time period must be non-negative
